### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **42** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d9682ffd7115b89a7f4c5c8dfe14691afc1ce7b`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d9682ffd7115b89a7f4c5c8dfe14691afc1ce7b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `64d63e745efdf0c17f48205969c04ad459542594` — the merge of head `417ed9b9c5afe55d27978b4738c76f1a20714f83` into base `7d9682ffd7115b89a7f4c5c8dfe14691afc1ce7b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 64d63e745efdf0c17f48205969c04ad459542594 && git checkout 64d63e745efdf0c17f48205969c04ad459542594
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7d9682ffd7115b89a7f4c5c8dfe14691afc1ce7b 417ed9b9c5afe55d27978b4738c76f1a20714f83 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7d9682ffd7115b89a7f4c5c8dfe14691afc1ce7b && git merge --no-ff 417ed9b9c5afe55d27978b4738c76f1a20714f83

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7d9682ffd7115b89a7f4c5c8dfe14691afc1ce7b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7d9682ffd7115b89a7f4c5c8dfe14691afc1ce7b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Package against package and built-ins, never the environment catalog (seat ruling 1).** `bareNamePackageHolders` walks the type's store, skips the bare slot (`key === name`) and reads only composite `packageId:name` slots (the stamp when present, else the key prefix) plus the install claims; `bareNameHoldersOtherThan` adds a built-in at the package door only. Pinned per type: an environment registration over a package's name coexists, an environment-only name is no holder, and an environment item under a package's name is no clash at the cold boot. TRUE, and the three places that state it (module doc, ADR P1.2, the anchor) agree.
- **Cold boot is one switch, shipping `'warn'` (seat ruling 2).** `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE: BareNameColdBootMode = 'warn'` in `bare-name-one-holder.ts` is read at exactly one call site, the engine plugin's `kernel:bootstrapped` hook, which hands it to `sealBareNameHoldersAtColdBoot(registry, mode, logger)`; `'refuse'` throws `BareNameConflictError` with `door: 'cold-boot'` from inside the hook, and the kernel's boot-path dispatch propagates (`hook-dispatch.ts`). Flipping it is the one constant plus the two pins that read the default (`it('the switch is "warn" ...')` and the dogfood boot case, which expects a boot and a WARN line); the `'refuse'` arm is pinned on its own through the exported function. A single point to flip. TRUE.
- **Family split (seat ruling 3).** The diff refuses `picklist`, `mapping`, `dataset` and nothing else (`BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES`, pinned by the `page` CONTROL); the ADR §3.4 note and P1.5 name the to-follow list (`api`, object-less `action`, function registry, `email_template`, `webhook`, `connector`, `flow`, `agent`, `skill`) and the security-seat carve-out. The three types match stage 1's silent rows; `analytics_cube` is left out for the measured reason (no reach). TRUE.
- **The refusal names both holders and the rename.** `bareNameConflictLine` carries the incoming package, the type, the name, `describeBareNameHolder(existing)` and the rename; the error's `conflicts[]` carries them structured; the cold-boot warning uses the same line. Install-local surfaces it as `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` with the message (dogfood pins `alpha`, `beta`, `"gamma_qa_shared_status"`); a third package is refused naming both earlier holders (pinned). The rename stands down for no namespace or a shareable one (`isShareableNamespace`) and when the name already carries the prefix. TRUE.
- **ADR-0146 `.custom` overrides unaffected.** A declared override (D2, `dataset` and `mapping` are overridable types) is a stored `sys_metadata` row bound to the pair; the pair is "never installed as code" (`marketplace-install-local-customization-pair.ts` header: its install writes each item through the save door), the ensure door installs an empty manifest through `installPackage` (claims nothing), and every hydration and write-through registers with no package (`protocol-registry-hydration.ts` 127/487/1302, `protocol.ts` 9876, `isArtifactBacked`'s note). The served override is read from rows (`isServedOverrideRowOf`), not the registry. So no path puts a pair's dataset or mapping into a composite slot or a claim, and the new seam never sees it. The one package-bound hydration site (`loadMetadataFromService`) covers `object, view, app, flow, hook` only. TRUE; the ADR addendum does not say this (nit below).
- **Unmanaged import unaffected.** `unmanagedImportCollisions` is untouched and reads rows plus `isArtifactBacked`; the import writes rows, which hydrate into the bare slot and are never judged. TRUE.
- **Kept behaviours.** Object-bound actions and jobs are outside the type list; same-package re-registration is excluded by `packages.includes(incomingPackageId)`; `picklistExtensions` declare no name; `collisionPolicy: 'warn'` is not consulted; every security-catalog path is untouched except one header sentence. Pinned as CONTROLs.
- **The fixture rename hides no consumer break (seat-accepted deviation).** The five `com.example.pull*` packages are the test's own and ship nowhere; the assertions still pin the same verdicts (`declares no mapping`, `declares no connectorSource`) against the renamed names. Across shipped first-party sets: the four examples hold 7 names with no duplicate; the blank template declares none; HotCRM's five packages hold 5 picklists, 3 mappings, 10 datasets with no duplicate inside the artifact. Across the two sets two dataset names coincide: `task_metrics` (HotCRM `src/sales/datasets/task.dataset.ts`, `examples/app-todo/src/datasets/task.dataset.ts`) and `opportunity_metrics` (HotCRM `src/sales/datasets/opportunity.dataset.ts`, `examples/app-crm/src/datasets/opportunity.dataset.ts`). No shipped composition installs HotCRM beside an example (dogfood boots the showcase alone; HotCRM's smoke boots HotCRM alone; `app-multi-package` declares none of the three types), so nothing shipped breaks at install; the coincidence is a should-fix on the changeset's measured-producers paragraph, below.
- **Precedent fit with `security-catalog-namespace.ts`.** Same vocabulary and shape (`*_TYPES`, `is*Type`, `COLLECTION_KEY`, `BUILT_IN_*`, the holder union, `describe*Holder`, `*HolderKey`, `declared*Names` reading the same sources as the engine seam, nested `plugins[]` one level as `registerPlugin` does), same door order in `installPackage` (after the default-record-page refusal, ahead of every mutation, no co-owner exemption, no downgrade), same item-seam placement (before stamp or store), claims noted on the restore point, forgotten at uninstall. The two differences are the ruled ones and each is stated in the module doc, the ADR and the precedent's amended header: the environment catalog is not a holder, and the cold boot is a seal plus a switch rather than a post-hydration boot check (claims are a Set because a boot registers every package before anything is judged). Sound.
- **ADR text matches the code**, with one breadth: §3.4's note and P1.2 say a built-in holder is refused "at managed install and at package registration", while the item seam asks `builtIns: false` (the module doc says "package door only", as the precedent's note did). Nit. P1.3's seal moment, P1.4's kept list, P1.5's to-follow list and P1.6's symbols match `registry.ts` and `plugin.ts`; the anchor names the file, ADR-0048 and ADR-0005 with the invariant's four ⛔s matching the module doc.

No `.describe()` text, no spec file, no error code or status moves. Nothing widened: `no (narrowing)` is the right spelling, matching the `_packageId` stamp refusal at the same door and the #22197 entry.

### ② Semver level

Both carriers read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, and the dispatch's warning against `yes (narrowing)` is honoured. `narrowed` is right by AGENTS.md step 3: a package registration that succeeded is now refused on a declared value, "a value refused". - The narrowing against ADR-0048 on `main`: §3.4 rests on every caller carrying its package id; stage 1 measured, on a booted two-package showcase in both orders, that a field's `picklist`, an import's `mappingName` and a dashboard's `datasetName` carry none and are served the first-registered holder silently (the picklist refusing a package's own values). Refusing a second holder where the package is registered is ruling C's phase-1 mechanism and takes away only a coexistence no consumer honoured. Holds.

The seal is placed where every package of the boot has registered (`AppPlugin.init`, the `kernel:ready` rehydrate), and a kernel that withholds the boot-phase hooks never seals, which the module doc and ADR state. Holds against `installPackage`'s refusal order and `registerItem`'s stamp-and-store order.
